blockingProblems: RIGOR, BLOCKING. The chapter reports critical exponents to six significant figures that it never defines. Line 95 gives nu = 0.63002(10), eta = 0.03627(10), omega = 0.832(6), then Delta_sigma = 0.518154(15) and Delta_epsilon = 1.41267(13). Nowhere in 4,110 words is nu identified as the correlation-length exponent, eta as the anomalous dimension, omega as the leading correction-to-scaling exponent, or 'scaling dimension' explained. The words 'susceptibility' and 'compressibility' appear ZERO times in the chapter, yet gamma is asserted at line 37 (gamma = 1), used with a prime at line 55, and made the subject of the Widom relation at line 61. delta is likewise never defined. A graduate student reaches line 95 and is handed a parade of unglossed Greek. This alone separates the chapter from any CUP/PUP/OUP monograph, all of which would carry a short exponent table or at minimum define each symbol at first use.

RIGOR, BLOCKING, and a flat error. Line 81: 'The critical exponents are these eigenvalues.' They are not. The eigenvalues y_i of the linearised flow determine the exponents through relations such as nu = 1/y_t and beta = (d - y_h)/y_t. The chapter has just spent two sections establishing that exponents are specific measured numbers (1/8, 1/3, 1/2, 0.63002), so identifying them outright with RG eigenvalues is not a permissible simplification, it is wrong, and it is wrong at the exact sentence where the book's central mechanism is supposed to land.

RIGOR, BLOCKING. The chapter's whole payoff, the homogeneous scaling form of the singular free energy, is never written down. Line 69 says coarse-graining 'forces the singular free energy to satisfy a self-similarity condition of exactly the homogeneous form Widom had assumed' and then stops. The chapter is willing to display the Hamiltonian, the Onsager T_c, the Landau expansion and the flow equation, so the omission is not a policy of restraint; it is the one equation the argument exists to produce, f_s(t,h) = b^(-d) f_s(b^(y_t) t, b^(y_h) h), and it is missing. Consequently not a single exponent relation is ever derived. The reader is told 'Every critical exponent is then some combination of a and b' (line 61) and 'since there are more exponents than free parameters, the exponents must satisfy relations' but is never shown one combination, not even 2 - alpha = d/y_t. This is gesturing at the physics, which is precisely the failure mode the chapter accuses itself of avoiding at line 103.

RIGOR. The verbal gloss of homogeneity at line 57 contradicts the equation it introduces. The prose says 'rescaling the arguments by a factor rescales the function by a power of that factor,' which describes ordinary homogeneity; the displayed formula Phi(lambda^a x, lambda^b y) = lambda Phi(x,y) rescales the two arguments by DIFFERENT powers and the function by lambda to the first power exactly. Neither the generalisation nor the normalisation of the degree to unity is explained, and the packet's own language ('a homogeneous function of x and y, with a positive degree of homogeneity') would have made the point correctly.

RIGOR. Notational collision, unremarked, three ways. beta is inverse temperature at line 25 (Boltzmann weight e^{-2\beta J L}); the order-parameter exponent at lines 37, 41, 43, 49, 51, 55, 61; and the RG beta function beta_i({g}) at line 79. A monograph in this field either flags the clash or avoids it. Here the reader meets 'beta = 1/8' and 'dg_i/d\ell = beta_i({g})' in the same chapter with no signal.

STRUCTURE, BLOCKING. The chapter opens on fluids (Guggenheim, eight substances) and then spends five sections on a lattice magnet, and never explains the bridge. The lattice-gas / Ising correspondence, the two-sentence mapping that makes a tank of argon and a lattice of arrows literally the same model, is never given. The phrase 'lattice gas' appears exactly once, buried in the title of the Essam-Fisher citation at line 49. In its place the chapter offers assertion: 'a lattice of two-valued arrows and a tank of liquid argon might be describing one thing' (line 49). The connection is only redeemed at line 83 by RG basins of attraction, which is the wrong tool for a correspondence that is exact and elementary. Eighty lines of the reader wondering why they are reading about magnets.

STRUCTURE. Chronological non sequitur at line 89. 'Wilson and Fisher supplied the calculational tool the following year.' The preceding paragraph is anchored on Fisher's 1974 review and Mermin-Wagner 1966. 'The following year' therefore reads as 1975 or 1967; the paper is 1972. The chapter has walked its reader forward to 1974 and then says 'the following year' meaning two years earlier. A copyeditor catches this; a referee should not have to.

STRUCTURE. Dangling promise. Line 9 announces that the Ising model 'is also the system the companion application simulates live, so it is worth setting up carefully.' The companion application is never mentioned again. Either the promise is paid inside the chapter or it should not be made in the third paragraph.

PROSE. A signposting tic, six occurrences in 4,110 words, roughly one every 700: 'it is worth keeping them apart' (7), 'it is worth setting up carefully' (9), 'It is worth stating plainly' (21), 'Two features of this argument deserve attention' (27), 'The chronology is worth getting right' (47), 'it is worth asking' (107). Each one is the author telling the reader that the next sentence matters instead of writing a sentence that matters. Line 103 is the worst instance because it is self-refuting: 'There is a structural analogy here that will run through the rest of this book, and it should be stated carefully rather than gestured at.' Announcing that you will not gesture is a gesture. Cut all six and the chapter loses nothing but throat-clearing.

PROSE. Flat and empty openers and fillers. Line 93, 'The abstraction is not vague,' is a negation standing in for a claim. Line 3, 'Their critical temperatures span a wide range,' says nothing a reader can use (the actual span, roughly 44 K for neon to 191 K for methane, would). Line 89, 'with characteristic dryness,' is unattributed editorial colour, and whose characteristic dryness is left unsaid. Line 107 opens with the fragment 'Which sets up a difficulty that is easy to miss,' a mannerism that reads as affectation in a university press monograph.
styleViolations: No hard-rule violations found on the mechanical checks, and this should be stated plainly: zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero occurrences of '--', zero bullet points, zero numbered lists in the body, no end-of-chapter summary or recap, and the chapter ends on a genuine forward-looking question (line 107) rather than a flat close. Verified by regex over the full file.

BORDERLINE, not a hard violation but a press would change it: the section heading 'Citations used in this chapter' (line 109) is a self-referential apparatus label. No CUP/PUP/OUP monograph prints that phrase; it prints 'Notes' or 'References'. The list itself is reference apparatus, not a recap, so it does not trip the summary rule.
factProblems: Line 81, FLATLY WRONG: 'The critical exponents are these eigenvalues.' Exponents are functions of the RG eigenvalues (nu = 1/y_t, beta = (d - y_h)/y_t), not the eigenvalues themselves. Nothing in the packet supports the identification.

Line 95, MISATTRIBUTED DERIVATION: the chapter says Delta_sigma = 0.518154(15) 'together with Delta_epsilon = 1.41267(13), which translate into nu = 0.62999(5), eta = 0.03631(3) and omega = 0.8303(18)'. Two dimensions cannot yield three exponents. The packet is explicit that omega comes from a third quantity, Delta_epsilon-prime = 3.8303(18), via Delta_epsilon-prime = 3 + omega. The chapter has silently dropped the operator that produces the number it prints.

Line 7, UNSOURCED AND SELF-INCONSISTENT: 'It took twenty-seven years... for the two observations to become one answer.' 1945 + 27 = 1972, but the chapter's own narrative places the answer at Wilson's renormalisation group in 1971 (section 'The flow'), which is twenty-six. The arithmetic is decorative precision with no referent in the packet or in the chapter's own account.

Line 21, NOT IN PACKET: 'The consequence was that the model was written off for about a decade as a failed account of ferromagnetism.' The packet's Ising claim covers the Lenz attribution, the 1D solution and the incorrect extrapolation. The decade-long reception history is nowhere in verifiedClaims.

Line 49, UNSUPPORTED PRIORITY CLAIM: Essam and Fisher's beta = 5/16 is called 'the first quantitative hint that a lattice of two-valued arrows and a tank of liquid argon might be describing one thing'. 'First' is a historical priority assertion. The packet supports the number and the chronology; it supports no claim of firstness.

Line 75, UNSUPPORTED CLAIM ABOUT A PERSON'S STATED VIEW: 'The block-spin picture has a defect that Kadanoff was clear about'. This asserts what Kadanoff himself acknowledged in print. The packet's Kadanoff entries say nothing about his own caveats.

Line 3, NOT IN PACKET: 'They differ in molecular mass by more than a factor of six' and 'Their critical temperatures span a wide range.' Both are quantitative statements about the eight substances; neither figure appears in verifiedClaims. The mass ratio happens to be right (neon 20.18 to xenon 131.29) but it is unsourced in the packet, and the temperature clause is a hedge with no number behind it.

Line 43, MISLEADING: 'Three different numbers, and the only obvious thing distinguishing the three cases is spatial dimension.' Mean-field theory is an approximation scheme, not a case with a spatial dimension. The claim only becomes true once the upper critical dimension is introduced, forty-six lines later at line 89, and the chapter uses it here as though already earned.

Line 89, IMPRECISE: 'Mean-field theory becomes exact at the upper critical dimension of four.' At exactly d = 4 the exponents carry logarithmic corrections; mean-field is exact ABOVE four and marginal at four. The packet's wording ('about the upper critical dimension four, where mean-field theory becomes exact') is the source, but a monograph must not print the marginal case as clean.

Line 101, UNSUPPORTED SUPERLATIVE: Anderson 1972 described as 'an essay that has framed most subsequent argument about emergence'. The packet says 'the canonical citation for emergence in phase-transition writing', which is narrower and defensible; 'most subsequent argument' is not.

POSITIVE FINDINGS, recorded so the author knows what to preserve. Every one of the packet's applicable corrections was applied correctly and visibly: the Sauer translation is cited as EPJ Special Topics 226, 539-549 (2017), not 2016 (line 111); the Ehrenfest gloss uses the safer 'do not describe real continuous transitions' wording rather than 'obsolete' (line 39); Rushbrooke's affiliation is given as the Chemistry Department, University of Oregon, not Newcastle (line 55); Essam and Fisher are placed at the Wheatstone Physics Laboratory, King's College, London (line 49); the scaling identity is credited to 'consideration of a heuristic model partition function rather than from the numerics' (line 49); the Padé analysis is correctly limited to producing 0.303 <= beta <= 0.318 and beta = 5/16; the five-and-a-half-month gap and the 1 August 1963 date are exact; Rushbrooke's first reference being Essam-Fisher is stated (line 55); Widom's homogeneity is correctly in temperature and DENSITY, not field (line 57); the Rushbrooke-before-Widom chronology is handled explicitly rather than backwards; the 2016 Kos paper is given its correct four authors and the 2012/2014 papers their correct six, avoiding both author-count traps; the 1982 Nobel is to Wilson alone with the 1980 Wolf Prize correctly shared; Onsager's 1948 announcement and Yang's 1952 first published derivation are correctly separated. The Peierls contour physics is also correct on the arithmetic: L broken bonds at 2J each, entropy exponential in L, weight bounded below one half.
whatWouldMakeItAAA:
"The chapter is close, which is why the failure is worth naming precisely rather than waving through. It fails on rigor and prose, not on integrity: the citation discipline is genuinely of press standard and every applicable correction in the packet was applied.

Five changes would make it AAA.

First, write the equation the chapter exists to produce. After line 69, display f_s(t,h) = b^(-d) f_s(b^(y_t) t, b^(y_h) h), set b = |t|^(-1/y_t), and derive 2 - alpha = d/y_t in three lines. Then show one scaling relation falling out, so the reader sees an inequality become an equality on the page instead of being told it happens. This also repairs the mismatch between the verbal gloss of homogeneity and the formula at line 57.

Second, define the exponents before using them. One compact paragraph after the Landau expansion at line 37: alpha for specific heat, beta for the order parameter, gamma for susceptibility (in a magnet) or compressibility (in a fluid), delta for the critical isotherm, nu for the correlation length, eta for the decay of the correlation function at criticality, omega for the leading correction to scaling. Then line 95's six-figure numbers mean something, and the 'susceptibility' the chapter currently never mentions enters the vocabulary before gamma does.

Third, give the lattice-gas correspondence two sentences somewhere before line 49. Occupied or empty site maps to up or down spin; chemical potential maps to field; the argon and the arrows are the same partition function. That converts the chapter's boldest assertion into its cleanest demonstration, and it is the missing joint between the fluid opening and the magnetic spine.

Fourth, fix line 81 to say that the exponents are determined by the eigenvalues (nu = 1/y_t), not that they are the eigenvalues; fix line 95 so omega is derived from Delta_epsilon-prime; fix 'the following year' at line 89 to name 1972 outright; and either pay off the companion-application promise from line 9 or delete it.

Fifth, cut all six instances of the 'it is worth' and 'deserve attention' signposting, and with them 'The abstraction is not vague,' 'with characteristic dryness,' and the 'Which sets up' fragment. The chapter's best sentences are declarative and cold ('Everything a real magnet has... has been deleted'; 'Homogeneity is assumed because it works'; 'The renormalisation group is a systematic procedure for deleting information'). It does not need to tell the reader when to pay attention. Trust the prose that is already there.

The opening and the closing are already at press standard and should not be touched. Guggenheim's figure as a cold open is the right instinct, and the final question about a network trained on exactly the data universality declares irrelevant is a genuinely strong hook."
